To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the synthesis of five- and six-coordinated tin(iv) compounds is achieved by the use of two heterocyclic ligands, 2-fu and 2-fuB, and that the compounds show different coordination modes of the heterocyclic ligand.

the synthesis of homoligand heteroaryl tin compounds using two O-substituents is possible and that the coordination of the counter ions to the hypercoordinate anionic tin(iv) compounds leads to a variety of structural motifs.

the reaction of the O-heterocycles 2-furyllithium and 2-benzo-furyllithum with SnCl2·2H2O in the presence of OEt2 or thf leads to the formation of homoleptic penta- or hexaorganostannyllithium complexes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new organotin(iv) complexes with heteroaryl ligands and their application in organic synthesis.
the synthesis and structural characterization of new tin(iv) compounds with O-heterocycle substituents.
the preparation of novel tin(iv) complexes with O-heteroaryl ligands and their structural characterization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the coordination of two O-heteroaromatic ligands to tin(iv) leads to the formation of homoleptic penta- and hexacordinate complexes.

a combination of two heteroaryls, such as 2-fuBn and 2-fu, leads to a coordination mode of the heteroaryl groups that differs from those observed when only one of the two ligands is attached to tin(iv).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the O-heterocycles 2-fu and 2-fuB as ligand donors in combination with the tin(iv) cation results in an interesting diversity of coordination patterns and geometries.
a variety of different tin(iv) complexes with O-heterocycles were obtained.
the coordination sphere of the tin atom in the present compounds can be described by a combination of the two ligand types.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the coordination of the lithium cation to the tin(iv) center is strongly affected by the steric bulk of the ligand, whereas the coordination of the potassium cation is mainly influenced by the solvent used.
the steric demand of the ligands and the coordination mode of the counterion play a decisive role in the coordination sphere of the tin center.
the coordination chemistry of the heteroaryl substituents is highly dependent on the steric demands of the ligands.
